name: obsidian-knight
note: Hand-written intent sidecar for the FROZEN rehearsal knight (rehearsal/knight/golem_knight.json). Landmarks are world coords read off that JSON. The attach list declares every intended FUSED join a competent knight author would author: the anatomy merges (limbs/armour into the torso at armpit + hip), the armour-plate contacts (breastplate to pauldron), and the full sword+grip assembly (hand around pommel AND grip; guard fused to blade and to the blade_flat cross-section workaround). Only pairs that actually interpenetrate are declared -- a declared-but-unfused pair would read as missing_fusion, so mere proximities (a forearm hovering by its own hilt) are left for the blend_ambiguity detector. The adjacencies deliberately NOT declared are the real defects and survive as anomalies: gauntlet.L~gauntlet.R (cross-plane lump), visor_ridge~torso (chin-on-chest), chest_plate~helm (helm bridges the chest, no neck void). Separately, expected_articulations declares the ONE girdle-shaped fusion the author intends: grip~blade (the sword is one rigid assembly, so grip fuses past the crossguard, 2 links apart) -- an articulated_fusion, not a defect. An articulation is a design intention; only a declared pair softens from unintended_fusion, so the undeclared chin-on-chest (visor_ridge~torso, also 2 links apart through the helm) stays a defect. Asserts A1-A7 adapt fable-b sec.2 to the real geometry; H is the knight's measured height (~2.905). The pack NAMES the three losses: hunch (A2 + suppressed burial), swallowed helm (A3 head-exposure + A4 shoulder-span + A7 heads-tall), cane-sword (A5 forward plant + A6 short length). A1 (blade ground contact) PASSES: the blade tip reaches the ground here (min_y 0.023 vs ground 0.02).
